provenance.source: NCERT Class 7 Chapter 11 / CBSE Curriculum Framework

nodes.title: Perimeter: Boundary Measurement
nodes.objective: Measure and calculate the total distance around a closed 2D shape.
nodes.concept: Perimeter is the length of the outer boundary.
nodes.explanation: Perimeter is the total path around the outside of a shape. For a rectangle with length 5 cm and width 3 cm, perimeter = 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 cm (linear measurement).

visual.text: Tap grid cells to reshape the rectangle. Watch how the boundary perimeter updates in linear cm.

nodes.title: Area: Surface Coverage
nodes.objective: Calculate the total surface enclosed inside a shape using unit squares.
nodes.concept: Area counts how many unit squares cover the flat surface.
nodes.explanation: Area measures the inside space. A rectangle with length 5 cm and width 3 cm contains 3 rows of 5 square centimeters: Area = 5 × 3 = 15 cm² (square units).

visual.text: Each small square is 1 cm². Count the rows and columns to see why multiplying gives total square units.

nodes.title: Perimeter vs Area Distinction
nodes.objective: Distinguish between boundary length (cm) and surface area (cm²) in real-world problems.
nodes.concept: Two shapes can have the same perimeter but different areas.
nodes.explanation: Perimeter is like putting a fence around a garden (1D linear length). Area is like laying grass turf over the soil (2D flat coverage). Never mix linear units (cm) with square units (cm²).

visual.text: Try a 4×4 square (Area = 16 cm², Perimeter = 16 cm). Shapes with identical perimeter can have completely different areas.

questions.prompt: A school sports ground needs a fence built around its outer edge. What mathematical measurement is needed?

options.feedback: Area measures the grass surface inside, not the outer fencing line.
Correct! A fence runs along the outer boundary, which is measured by perimeter.
Volume is for 3D solid capacity (like water in a tank), not a flat boundary.
A diagonal only cuts across the middle; it does not measure the full border.

questions.prompt: A rectangular garden has a length of 6 m and a breadth of 4 m. What is its perimeter?

options.feedback: 24 m² is the Area (6 × 4). Perimeter is the boundary distance: 2 × (6 + 4) = 20 m.
A rectangle has 4 sides, not 2. Add both lengths and both breadths: 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 m.
Correct! Perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth) = 2 × (6 + 4) = 20 m.
Check your formula: 2 × (6 + 4) = 2 × 10 = 20 m.

questions.prompt: A piece of wire 20 cm long is bent to form a square. What is the length of each side?

options.feedback: A square has 4 equal sides, not 2. Divide the total perimeter 20 cm by 4.
Exactly! In a square, all 4 sides are equal: 20 cm ÷ 4 = 5 cm per side.
If each side were 4 cm, perimeter would be 4 × 4 = 16 cm, but the wire is 20 cm.
The whole wire is only 20 cm; one side cannot be longer than the entire wire.

questions.prompt: Which task requires calculating AREA rather than perimeter?

options.text: Putting a lace border around a square dupatta
options.feedback: A lace runs along the outer boundary, which is perimeter.

options.text: Running one full lap around the outside of a football pitch
options.feedback: Running the track around the edge is perimeter.

options.text: Tiling the flat floor of a classroom with ceramic tiles
options.feedback: Correct! Tiling covers the entire 2D surface inside, which requires Area.

options.text: Building a brick wall along the edge of a garden
options.feedback: The boundary wall edge is perimeter.

questions.prompt: What is the area of a square tile with a side length of 7 cm?

options.feedback: 28 cm is the perimeter (4 × 7). Area is side × side = 7 × 7 = 49 cm².
Correct! Area of a square = side × side = 7 cm × 7 cm = 49 cm².
Do not multiply by 2. Multiply the side by itself: 7 × 7 = 49 cm².
Area must be expressed in square units (cm²), not linear units (cm).

questions.prompt: A grid paper rectangle covers 4 rows of 6 squares. Each square is 1 cm × 1 cm. What is the total area?

options.feedback: 20 cm is the boundary perimeter (2 × (6 + 4)). Area is the total number of squares inside: 4 × 6 = 24 cm².
Correct! 4 rows with 6 squares each make 4 × 6 = 24 unit squares = 24 cm².
Do not add rows and columns (4 + 6). Multiply them to find the grid count: 4 × 6 = 24 cm².
Area must always have square units (cm²).

questions.prompt: Which unit is appropriate for measuring the surface area of a student notebook cover?

options.feedback: cm is a 1D linear unit for length and perimeter, not 2D area.
Correct! Area measures 2D space and is always written in square units like cm².
cm³ is a 3D unit for volume, not flat 2D area.
kg measures mass/weight, not geometric surface area.

questions.prompt: Rectangle A has dimensions 8 cm × 2 cm. Rectangle B has dimensions 5 cm × 5 cm. Which statement is true?

options.text: Both have the same perimeter (20 cm), but Rectangle B has a larger area (25 cm² vs 16 cm²)
options.feedback: Brilliant! Perimeter of both is 20 cm, but Rectangle B encloses more surface (25 cm² > 16 cm²). Same perimeter does NOT mean same area.

options.text: Because they have the same perimeter, their areas must be identical
options.feedback: A common mistake! Shapes with identical perimeter often have very different areas.

options.text: Rectangle A has a larger area because 8 is larger than 5
options.feedback: Compare total area: 8 × 2 = 16 cm², whereas 5 × 5 = 25 cm².

options.text: Rectangle B has a larger perimeter
options.feedback: Check perimeters: 2 × (8 + 2) = 20 cm, and 4 × 5 = 20 cm. Perimeters are equal.

questions.prompt: A farmer needs to: (1) put a barbed-wire fence along the boundary, and (2) spread organic fertilizer over the field. What measurements does he need for (1) and (2)?

options.feedback: The fence surrounds the border (Perimeter) while fertilizer covers the soil surface (Area).
Correct! Wire fence = boundary length (Perimeter). Fertilizer = surface coverage (Area).
Fertilizer covers the interior surface of the ground, which requires Area.
The fence only goes along the outer edge, which requires Perimeter.
